_comment: Inline policy for the IAM User(s) whose ARN you add to ALLOWED_AGENT_ARNS
(and, if it's also the trusted executor, MCP_EXECUTOR_ARN) in the gate's
config. This is the permission side of that trust: ALLOWED_AGENT_ARNS only
controls who the gate will ACCEPT a presigned identity from — it grants no
AWS permissions itself. This policy is what actually lets that identity
call AWS. See docs/agent-contract.md for the SigV4 handshake and
docs/mcp-gateway.md / deploy/scp/ for the account-wide backstop that
denies these same actions to every OTHER principal.
Prefer an IAM Role (IRSA on the cluster ServiceAccount, matching how the
rest of deploy/k8s/ is set up) over a long-lived IAM User wherever
possible — this file is provided as an inline User policy only because
that's what was asked for; attach it the same way to a Role instead if you
can (aws iam put-role-policy).
Replace ACCOUNT_ID before attaching:
aws iam put-user-policy --user-name mcp-agent-user \
--policy-name mcp-approval-gate-agent \
--policy-document file://agent-user-inline-policy.json
Action list intentionally mirrors deploy/scp/deny-ec2-mutations-except-
gate.json's allowlist (the v1 EC2 scope) so the two stay in sync — an
action added to one without the other either can't be called (missing
here) or is silently un-gated at the account level (missing there).
AllowGatedResourceCreation requires aws:RequestTag/gateTicketId — but only
on the subset of actions that actually accept a TagSpecifications
parameter. Do NOT add that condition to AllowGatedExistingResourceActions:
those calls (StopInstances, TerminateInstances, Authorize/RevokeSecurity-
GroupIngress/Egress, ...) carry no request-tag parameter at all, so a
requires-the-tag condition on them would deny this identity too, not just
unapproved callers. See docs/agent-contract.md's 'Strong enforcement'
section for the full explanation.
The two mutating statements are scoped to arn:aws:ec2:ca-central-1:ACCOUNT_ID:* — this
account, any region, any EC2 resource type/id (the trailing bare '*'
covers instance/*, security-group/*, volume/*, snapshot/*, key-pair/*,
elastic-ip/*, etc. all at once, which RunInstances in particular needs
since it touches several resource types in one call). Note the region
field is a wildcard '*', not empty (':::' would match a literal empty
region, which no EC2 resource has, and would silently make the statement
match nothing). sts:GetCallerIdentity and ec2:Describe* are left at
Resource: "*" deliberately — neither supports resource-level permissions,
so any other value would just break them, not narrow them.
